requirements.title: Agent Decision Reduction Profile: Causa Rehearsal and Competition
requirements.heading: # Agent Decision Reduction Profile: Causa Rehearsal and Competition

obligations.text: Minimize avoidable agent choices, integration churn, and repeated release candidates while preserving correctness and the reversible/experimental boundaries in DESIGN-DECISION-BOUNDARIES.md.
First inventory current Praxis, Ordo, Dokimos, Percepta and related contracts.
For each AR requirement, record existing implementation, gap, owning repository, test plan, and dependency.
Place resulting work in each owner's documented Praxis input path.
Do not mark requirements implemented merely because this document exists.
The reported ARCH-002 trial found 29 architecture violations in 68 unguided trials versus 0 in 71 trials with the four-tier architecture brief.
Additional Ordo enforcement showed no measured improvement and reportedly increased cost by 7%.
Continuous agents reportedly reduced cost per accepted requirement by 40.9%.
These are experiment-specific observations, not universal guarantees; retain raw trial evidence and study context-compaction effects separately.
AR-027..AR-035 add to AR-001..AR-026 and refine them only where stated.
AR-019..AR-026 refine AR-001..AR-018 when there is tension.

In particular AR-003 protects genuine approval authority, not agent-maintained pseudo-authority; AR-006 concerns domain correctness, not universal typed agent messages; AR-013 allows test prioritization, not skipping mandatory CI.
These requirements do not establish that any release or implementation is complete.
These requirements come from defects that Rehearsal 5 found while it ran (`kemiller2002/indy-init-rehearsal-005`, clock 2026-10-27T20:08:38Z to 2026-10-28T03:08:38Z).
They apply from the next baseline re-pin.
They do not change the frozen Rehearsal 5 baseline (`aab8f80`), and they do not claim that Rehearsal 5 met them.
Remove or weaken a mandatory UI requirement: preservation gate fails.
Modify baseline content while retaining a prior digest: integrity gate fails.
Swap semantic roles or negate a requirement without removing its keywords: semantic preservation review detects it.
Forge an agent-authored operator approval: approval gate fails.
Skip or disable the CI gate: acceptance remains blocked.
Use mock data in place of a required live test: acceptance remains blocked.
Present source code without behavior evidence: no PASS is granted.
Re-run a task with the same pinned inputs: evidence and decisions remain traceable.
Modify an unrelated file: scope guard reports it.
Compare matched constrained/unconstrained agent runs and publish correctness and cost without invented measurements.

requirements.title: Multi-writer persistence semantics
requirements.heading: **AR-035 [P0] Multi-writer persistence semantics.** Persistence MUST be proven under concurrent writers: several tabs, devices and page loads, with lost answers and reloads. Write markers MUST be unique across writers, and a save MUST NOT count as confirmed until the committed content has been read back and verified. After a write is sent, any answer the code does not recognise MUST be treated as "may have saved", never as "not written". Each tab MUST hold its own state in memory, and tabs MUST share nothing but GitHub (PERSIST-002 to PERSIST-004). Rehearsal 5 found and fixed the first three during the run (review findings F-1, F-2, R2-F1); its fourth, device-local durable state shared by several tabs (R2-F2), is superseded by ADR-R7-001 after Rehearsal 6's R6-D-002.

requirements.title: Each browser tab holds its own investigation state
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-002: Each browser tab holds its own investigation state [P0]

obligations.text: Each browser tab MUST hold its own, independent investigation state in F# WebAssembly memory: the investigations it has loaded, the branch head each was loaded or saved at, its unsaved changes, and its save state.
A tab MUST NOT read or write another tab's state.
Opening the same investigation in two tabs gives two independent copies; a change in one tab MUST NOT appear in the other until it has been saved to GitHub and the other tab loads it from GitHub.
Navigation between routes inside one tab MUST keep that tab's state in memory, so moving between investigations or views never loses unsaved changes.
Acceptance: PAT-01 verifies tab independence in a real browser.

requirements.title: No shared browser storage for investigations
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-003: No shared browser storage for investigations [P0]

obligations.text: Investigation documents, events, snapshots, manifests, unsaved changes, pending commands, save state, branch heads and write markers MUST NOT be written to localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, Cache Storage, the Origin Private File System, cookies, a service worker, a shared worker or a BroadcastChannel.
Only non-investigation preferences, such as tour dismissal (UI-012) or theme, may use browser storage, and they MUST NOT contain investigation content, repository paths or credentials.
Credentials stay memory-only (EXT-DATA-004, OD-INDY-10).
The browser's ordinary HTTP cache of the application's static assets is not investigation storage.

Acceptance: PAT-01 inspects every browser store after edits and saves and verifies that none holds investigation content, and PAT-13 verifies that the production artifact contains no call that writes investigation content to a browser store.

requirements.title: No cross-tab locking or coordination
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-004: No cross-tab locking or coordination [P0]

obligations.text: Correctness MUST NOT depend on cross-tab locking or messaging.
The application MUST NOT use `navigator.locks` (Web Locks), a storage lease or a cross-tab message channel to coordinate investigation writes.
Two tabs that save are two independent GitHub writers, and their concurrency is resolved only by the GitHub rules in PERSIST-007 to PERSIST-013.
Acceptance: PAT-11 verifies that every persistence test passes with `navigator.locks` removed from the page, and PAT-13 verifies that the production artifact references no Web Locks API.

requirements.title: GitHub is the authoritative durable store
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-005: GitHub is the authoritative durable store [P0]

obligations.text: The connected GitHub repository branch MUST be the only durable store of Causa investigations.
An investigation is opened by reading it from GitHub at a branch head and verifying it as a reader would (causa-data v1.0.0 §11).
The tab records the commit it read as the investigation's base head.
Branch-head reads MUST bypass HTTP caches, and file reads MUST name the commit they read.
Acceptance: PAT-10 verifies that an investigation opened in a new tab equals its last confirmed commit on GitHub.

requirements.title: One atomic commit per save, with an expected head
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-006: One atomic commit per save, with an expected head [P0]

obligations.text: Every save MUST publish exactly one GitHub commit through one GraphQL `createCommitOnBranch` mutation, as OD-INDY-9 defines.
The commit MUST contain the investigation's events append, manifest and snapshot together.
Its `expectedHeadOid` MUST be the branch head the change was decided at, or the head it was rebased onto under PERSIST-009.
A save MUST NOT use per-file Contents API writes, a forced ref update, or any write without an expected head.
Before sending, the adapter MUST check that the commit changes files only under the investigation's own path prefix (causa-data v1.0.0 §9.4.4).
A tab MUST have at most one commit mutation in flight at a time; further save requests in that tab wait in memory until it settles.
Acceptance: PAT-02 records every mutation the application sends and verifies each one against this requirement.

requirements.title: A save is confirmed only after GitHub confirms it
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-007: A save is confirmed only after GitHub confirms it [P0]

obligations.text: A save is confirmed only when GitHub has returned the new commit for that mutation and a re-read at that commit returns the bytes the save wrote (causa-data v1.0.0 §9.4.3).
Only a confirmed save may move the investigation to Saved and advance its base head.
Changes made in the tab while the save was in flight MUST remain unsaved after it is confirmed.
Acceptance: PAT-02 and PAT-10 verify that Saved appears only after the read-back, and PAT-12 verifies that no other transition reaches Saved.

When GitHub refuses a mutation because the branch head is no longer the expected head, the application MUST classify the answer as a stale head: nothing was written, and the change stays unsaved in memory.
It MUST classify each provider answer from its typed content, and MUST keep a stale head distinct from a network failure, an authentication or permission failure, a rate limit and a validation error.
A network failure MUST NOT be reported as a stale head or a conflict.
Acceptance: PAT-03 verifies each classification with the stateful GitHub fake and against the live test repository.

requirements.title: Rebase automatically over unrelated changes
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-009: Rebase automatically over unrelated changes [P0]

obligations.text: After a stale head, the application MUST read the new branch head and compare the investigation's files at the base head and at the new head.
When those files are unchanged, the branch moved only for unrelated changes, such as another investigation saved by this tab, another tab or another device.
The application MUST then re-verify the remote history, keep the same events, manifest and snapshot, and send the commit again with the new head as `expectedHeadOid`, without asking the user.
While it does so, the investigation stays Saving.
Acceptance: PAT-04 verifies that a change saves without user action after unrelated commits advance the branch, and that the unrelated commits stay on the branch.
One save request MUST make at most three automatic rebase attempts, so it sends at most four commit mutations in total.
Every attempt MUST follow a fresh read of the branch head.
When the limit is reached, the investigation MUST move to Save failed, with the cause that the repository kept changing, and keep the change unsaved in memory until the user asks to save again.
Acceptance: PAT-08 verifies that a branch that advances before every attempt receives no more than four mutations for one save request.

requirements.title: Preserve unsaved changes when the same investigation changed remotely
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-011: Preserve unsaved changes when the same investigation changed remotely [P0]

obligations.text: When the investigation's own files differ between the base head and the new head, another writer has saved the same investigation, and this is a genuine conflict.
This includes another tab of the same user.
The application MUST NOT rebase, merge or overwrite automatically.
It MUST move the investigation to Conflict and keep every unsaved change unchanged in memory, still visible in the tab.
An investigation deleted or rewritten on the branch is also a conflict.
Acceptance: PAT-05 verifies that the unsaved change is kept, nothing is sent, and the other writer's commit stays on the branch.

requirements.title: Resolve a genuine conflict only by explicit user choice
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-012: Resolve a genuine conflict only by explicit user choice [P0]

obligations.text: A conflict MUST stay in Conflict until the user chooses a resolution.
The application MUST offer three actions: review the differences, reapply my changes to the GitHub version, and discard my changes and load the GitHub version.
Reapply MUST load the GitHub version and re-decide each unsaved command, in its original order, through the F# domain engine at that version.
Accepted commands become unsaved changes on the new base head; refused commands MUST be listed with the engine's reason and MUST NOT be applied.
Reapply MUST NOT save; the user saves the result.
Discard MUST ask for confirmation first.
The application MUST NOT offer any action that replaces the GitHub version with the tab's version.
Acceptance: PAT-05 verifies each action and that no action overwrites the other writer's commit.

requirements.title: Never silently overwrite another commit
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-013: Never silently overwrite another commit [P0]

obligations.text: No write may remove, replace or hide a commit made by another writer.
The application MUST NOT force-push, reset a ref, delete and recreate files, or write against a head it has not read from GitHub in the current tab session.
Every other writer's commit MUST remain reachable from the branch head after any sequence of saves, rebases, reconciliations and conflict resolutions.
Acceptance: PAT-02, PAT-04 and PAT-05 verify after each scenario that every commit made by every writer is still reachable from the branch head.
Each tab MUST create a random session identifier in memory when it starts.
Each commit mutation MUST carry a write marker made of that identifier and a sequence number, as a trailer in the commit message.
Markers are audit metadata used only for reconciliation (causa-data v1.0.0 §9.4.5), and MUST be unique across tabs, devices and page loads.
Acceptance: PAT-02 verifies marker uniqueness across concurrent tabs and reloads.

requirements.title: Reconcile an unknown commit outcome before retrying
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-015: Reconcile an unknown commit outcome before retrying [P0]

obligations.text: When a mutation may have reached GitHub but no recognised answer came back, the outcome is unknown.
This covers a timeout, a lost response, a dropped connection after sending, and any answer the code does not recognise.
The investigation MUST move to Unknown commit outcome and MUST NOT send another mutation for it until reconciliation decides the outcome.
Reconciliation reads the branch head and the commits after the expected head.
If a commit carries this save's marker and its tree holds the written bytes, the save is confirmed.
If a commit carries the marker but the bytes differ, the investigation moves to Save failed and is not reported as saved.
If the branch head still equals the expected head and no commit carries the marker, nothing was written, and the save may be sent again within the PERSIST-010 limit.
If the head moved and no commit carries the marker, the change was not written and the stale-head rules apply.
If the expected head is no longer an ancestor of the branch head, the investigation moves to Save failed with the cause that the branch history was rewritten.
If a reconciliation read fails, the investigation stays Unknown commit outcome.
Acceptance: PAT-06 verifies every branch of this rule with injected lost answers.

requirements.title: Bounded retries and no tight loops
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-016: Bounded retries and no tight loops [P0]

obligations.text: Automatic network activity for one save request MUST be bounded.
Commit mutations are limited by PERSIST-010.

Reconciliation of one unknown outcome MUST make at most three automatic reads, at least 2 seconds, 4 seconds and 8 seconds apart, plus one read each time the browser goes from offline to online; after that it waits for the user to choose Check again.
A save that fails before it is sent MUST NOT be retried automatically.
Under a network that fails every request, one save request MUST cause at most four commit mutations and at most four reconciliation reads in 60 seconds.
Acceptance: PAT-08 counts requests for 60 seconds under total network failure and under constant branch advance.

requirements.title: An already loaded investigation stays visible offline
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-017: An already loaded investigation stays visible offline [P0]

obligations.text: When the network is lost, every investigation already loaded in the tab MUST stay visible in every view, from the tab's in-memory projection.
An investigation that is not loaded MUST show as unavailable offline, never as empty or missing.
Acceptance: PAT-07 verifies that the loaded investigation's views render offline and an unloaded one shows unavailable offline.

requirements.title: Editing while disconnected stays in session memory
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-018: Editing while disconnected stays in session memory [P0]

obligations.text: If the application allows edits while disconnected, those edits exist only in the tab's memory and MUST be shown as not saved.
While the application knows it is offline, a save request MUST NOT send a mutation; it fails immediately and the investigation shows Offline.
There is no offline synchronization queue: after the connection returns, the application MUST NOT replay or send saves automatically, and the changes are saved only by a new save request.
Acceptance: PAT-07 verifies that a save requested offline sends no request, shows Offline, and that nothing is sent when the connection returns until the user saves.

requirements.title: Warn before leaving with unsaved changes
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-019: Warn before leaving with unsaved changes [P0]

obligations.text: While any investigation in the tab is Unsaved, Saving, Offline, Conflict, Unknown commit outcome or Save failed, the application MUST register a `beforeunload` handler so that browsers which support it warn before the tab is closed, reloaded or navigated away.
It MUST remove the handler when every investigation is Saved.
In-application actions that would drop unsaved changes, such as disconnecting, switching repository or discarding, MUST ask for confirmation.
Acceptance: PAT-09 verifies the leave warning in Chromium and the confirmations in every supported browser.

requirements.title: Unsaved work does not survive browser termination
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-020: Unsaved work does not survive browser termination [P0]

obligations.text: Closing, reloading or crashing the tab, or the browser or operating system discarding it, destroys unsaved changes.
The application provides no local crash recovery of investigation content, and MUST NOT imply that it does.
Safari on iPad may not show a leave warning, so the save-state indicator is the primary safeguard.
The Connect screen and the in-application help MUST state that unsaved changes exist only in the current tab and are lost when it closes.
After a reload, the tab starts from GitHub.
Acceptance: PAT-09 verifies the statement is present and reachable by keyboard and screen reader, and PAT-10 verifies that a reload shows only confirmed GitHub state.
Opening an investigation in a new tab, after a reload, or on another device MUST load the latest confirmed commit from GitHub and verify it.
The investigation MUST show Saved at that commit.
It MUST contain every confirmed save and nothing that was not confirmed.
Acceptance: PAT-10 verifies reopening after saves from several tabs.

requirements.title: One save state per investigation
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-022: One save state per investigation [P0]

obligations.text: Each investigation in a tab MUST have its own save state.
A page MUST show the save state of the investigation it displays, never another investigation's.
A workspace-level summary MAY count the investigations in each state, but MUST NOT state a fact that contradicts them.
Acceptance: PAT-02 and PAT-05 verify, with two investigations changed in one tab, that each page shows its own state.

requirements.title: Truthful save state is structural
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-023: Truthful save state is structural [P0]

obligations.text: The save state MUST be computed by one F# state machine, and the user interface MUST render only that machine's projection.
Saved MUST be constructible only from a confirmation produced by the PERSIST-007 read-back.
Adapters, view code and test fixtures in the production build MUST NOT be able to construct it.
Every illegal input to the machine MUST fail closed with a typed fault and leave the state unchanged.
Acceptance: PAT-12 verifies every state and input pair and verifies that application code cannot construct Saved.

requirements.title: Failure causes are reported truthfully
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-024: Failure causes are reported truthfully [P0]

obligations.text: Every save-state message MUST state the cause the application actually determined.
A network failure is never described as another writer's change.
A conflict is never offered for a failure that only needs the network.
Discard is offered only in Conflict and after an explicit request.

Acceptance: PAT-07 verifies, with the network failing on the rebase path, that the investigation shows Offline or Unknown commit outcome and never Conflict, and PAT-14's message check rejects a false cause.

The acceptance tests MUST run against a stateful GitHub fake that enforces `expectedHeadOid`, keeps real commit ancestry, accepts commits from simulated other writers, and can lose an answer after applying or before applying a mutation.
The tests MUST also run against the real GitHub test repository.
A fake-only pass MUST NOT be reported as live verification (UI-015, PF-020).

It MUST NOT copy, vendor, translate or adapt application source code, tests or scripts from Causa or any earlier rehearsal repository (indy-init-rehearsal-001 to indy-init-rehearsal-006).
Earlier rehearsals are historical evidence about failures, not code to reuse.
A published library MUST NOT be used to store investigation content in the browser, whatever its features.

Every displayed investigation MUST show a save-state indicator in its header, built from Forma components: a Forma status lozenge for the state, Forma operation status for the explanation and actions of Unknown commit outcome and Save failed, Forma conflict review for Conflict, and Forma freshness for the time of the last confirmed save.
Colours MUST come from semantic Forma theme tokens (UI-016).
The indicator MUST show exactly one of seven states: Saved, Unsaved, Saving, Offline, Conflict, Unknown commit outcome and Save failed.
Each state MUST be named in text and marked with the lozenge glyph, never by colour alone.
Text MUST meet 4.5:1 contrast and the indicator's non-text marks 3:1.
A change of state MUST be announced through a polite status live region; Conflict, Unknown commit outcome and Save failed MUST be announced assertively.
The indicator MUST stay visible and readable at 320px width, at 200% text size and in iPad portrait and landscape.
Acceptance: PAT-15 verifies every state's rendering, contrast, announcement and reflow, with screenshots of each state from the deployed exact SHA.

requirements.title: Meaning of each save state
requirements.heading: ## PERSIST-031: Meaning of each save state [P0]

obligations.text: The seven states have these entry conditions, words and actions:
Saved: the last save was confirmed under PERSIST-007 and the tab holds no unsaved change.
The lozenge reads "Saved", and the freshness line gives the commit time.
No action is offered.
Unsaved: the tab holds changes that have not been sent, and the application is online.
The text says the changes exist only in this tab.
The action is Save.
Saving: a commit mutation is being prepared or is in flight, or an automatic rebase or reconciliation read is running.
The text says the change is being saved to GitHub and is not yet confirmed.
No save action is offered.
Offline: the application is offline and the tab holds unsaved changes.
The text says the changes exist only in this tab and cannot be saved until the connection returns.
Save is offered only after the connection returns.
Conflict: PERSIST-011 applies.
The text says another writer changed this investigation on GitHub, nothing of this tab's change was written, and the tab's changes are kept.
The actions are the three of PERSIST-012.
Unknown commit outcome: PERSIST-015 applies.
The text says the save may or may not have reached GitHub and that the application is checking.
Save is not offered; Check again is offered after the automatic reads are spent.
Save failed: GitHub refused the save for a reason other than a stale head, the rebase limit was reached, or a reconciliation found a mismatch or rewritten history.
The text names the cause and says the changes are kept in this tab.
The action is Retry when a retry can succeed, or Reconnect when the credential was refused.
When the application is offline and the tab holds no unsaved change, the indicator stays Saved and the workspace header shows that the application is offline.
Acceptance: PAT-15 verifies each state's entry condition, words and actions, and PAT-12 verifies that the machine reaches each state only from its entry condition.
The words saved, synced, stored and safe MUST NOT describe an investigation in any state other than Saved.
The interface MUST NOT say that a change is saved locally, saved on this device, queued, or will be saved later.
Offline and Unsaved MUST say that the change exists only in this tab.
Retry and Check again MUST be shown only when they perform a real action (UI-010).
Acceptance: PAT-15 verifies the text of every state against this list, and PAT-14 verifies that no requirement or interface copy in the candidate uses a forbidden phrase.

requirements.title: PAT-08 no uncontrolled retry loops

The rules:
**Hash routes.** The route follows `#/` in `index.html#/...`, with relative links and no `<base href>`, so a reloaded deep link never 404s on GitHub Pages (D-203, Limen DF-LIMEN-2026-0006).
**IDs.** Every `{...Id}` is the entity's GUID (`FSHARP-TYPE-SHAPES.md`); `{branchId}` is the counterfactual BranchId and `{version}` is an aggregate version (`int`).
No other identifier, and no evidence content, appears in a URL.
**Repository.** Investigation routes carry the persistence repository as the `repo` query parameter (`owner/name`), so the link resolves in another browser (OQ-048).
**Version.** `at` (`int`) on any investigation-scoped route opens that view as of an aggregate version, visibly read-only (S14).
Without it the view shows the current version.
**Canonical form.** The canonical URL holds declared parameters only, in the order listed, with defaults omitted, sets sorted and de-duplicated, and `%20` with upper-case hex.
**History.** Moving between rows of the table, or to another entity, pushes history.
Changing a query parameter of the current row replaces it.
**Missing targets.** An unknown ID, an unreadable repository, or data not available offline shows not found, not permitted or unavailable offline with a way back, never another record (P34.19).
A superseded entity shows as superseded.
**Inventory.** `.echelon/routes.json` (`echelon.routes/v1`) lists exactly these routes and is regenerated from the route table (Limen `Inventory.render`).
**Copy link.** Screens marked ✓ offer a Copy link action that copies the canonical URL.
